reference_fields: Fruit Quality Characteristics of New Peach and Nectarine Varieties: Selena and Silverglo
Fruit Notes Volume 84, Number 1, Winter 2019 article reporting fruit-quality characteristics for Rutgers Selena peach and Silverglo nectarine in southern New Jersey

locations.name: Rutgers Fruit and Ornamental Research Extension Center, Cream Ridge, New Jersey

categories.name: Rutgers Selena and Silverglo fruit quality observations
categories.description: Fruit Notes reports southern New Jersey fruit-quality observations for Rutgers Selena peach and Silverglo nectarine

rows.name: NJ 358
rows.category: Rutgers Selena and Silverglo fruit quality observations
rows.harvest_time: September 5 to 20 in southern New Jersey
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Selena as a late-season yellow peach with excellent firmness, red-on-yellow skin color, high sugar with acidity, good hang time, and good commercial potential. The article reports three-year averages of 9.9 lb firmness, 3.1 inch diameter, 244 g mass, 5.7 g/l total titratable acidity, and 12.1 Brix total soluble solids

rows.name: NJN 103
rows.category: Rutgers Selena and Silverglo fruit quality observations
rows.harvest_time: August 5 to 20 in southern New Jersey
rows.description: Fruit Notes describes Silverglo as a firm white nectarine that is larger and more attractive than other white nectarines during its early harvest window, with good commercial potential. The article reports three-year averages of 10.1 lb firmness, 2.7 inch diameter, 191 g mass, 7.4 g/l total titratable acidity, and 10.5 Brix total soluble solids
